The agent nodes drive YOUR OWN local coding agent over ACP (real subprocess, real cost); the real GitHub steps (reading the diff, posting a review) require your GitHub access on your machine. Agent nodes produce a structured {stopReason,text} turn result, NOT a scalar; the branch therefore gates on a SUPPLIED typed input (mode) rather than a score parsed from agent content — automated gating on agent content (e.g. parsing a quality number) needs a future parse/command step. mode=strict routes to deep-review; the default (standard) routes to standard-review — both ends are reachable.
name: PR Triage
description: Template: parallel ACP probes assess an open PR, a join agent summarizes after all probes finish, and a typed branch on the supplied "mode" input routes to "deep-review" (mode=strict) or "standard-review". Honestly a template — running it needs a real local agent (and, for the real GitHub steps, GitHub access); the graph itself calls nothing.

agent.prompt: Read this pull request (title, description, and diff) and state, in one sentence, what change the author intends to make and why. Do not evaluate quality yet — only capture the intent.

Assess the quality of this pull request diff: correctness, test coverage, clarity, and adherence to the surrounding code. Summarize the main quality signals and any blocking concerns in a few sentences.

Determine whether this pull request likely conflicts with the current state of the target branch (overlapping edits, stale APIs, merge markers). Explain briefly whether a conflict is likely and where.

Given the extracted intent, the quality assessment, and the conflict assessment gathered so far, write a concise triage summary for a maintainer: what the PR does, its main risks, and a recommended next action.
